title: Gemini decides, SMS delivers: closing the last mile of workflow automation in 2026
headline: Governing customer-facing AI agents and SMS workflows
summary: This opinion piece examines the integration of AI decision-making tools like Gemini with transactional messaging to automate customer-facing workflows. It highlights operational governance risks when AI agents trigger external communications without adequate oversight or registered sender IDs. The article sets out a practical governance checklist for IT leaders deploying autonomous communication agents.
why_it_matters: Organisations connecting AI agents to customer-facing messaging must implement strict consent records, registered sender IDs, and human-in-the-loop controls to prevent trust failures and security incidents.

quotes.text: Agents that can text customers need tighter rules than agents that summarise meetings.
An automated system needs more than permission to send a message; it needs clear limits, monitoring and a reliable way to stop when something goes wrong.

dates_mentioned.what: ACMA SMS Sender ID Register requirement took effect
dates_mentioned.quote: Since 1 July 2026, only sender IDs registered on the ACMA SMS Sender ID Register display as the brand name on Australian handsets.

classification.significance_reason: Provides practical governance and compliance recommendations for Australian IT teams connecting AI agents to messaging, referencing ACMA and Spam Act requirements.
